name: 142. Gemini embeddings request-level taskType and title fan-out (#7812) (gemini-embedding-tasktype)
description: Issue #7812: a /v1/embeddings request to gemini-embedding-001 with several inputs and a request-level taskType (and/or title) must embed EVERY input with that task type. v2.2.4 applied it to the first entry only (the converter deleted the key from a map shared across the loop); after the multimodal-embedding refactor the Gemini-native extra-param spelling `taskType`/`title` was dropped from every entry, and with x-bf-passthrough-extra-params it leaked to the batch top level, where Gemini rejects unknown fields. Nothing errors in the silent case: the vectors come from the wrong embedding space (RETRIEVAL_QUERY instead of RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT), so the response body cannot tell right from wrong. 142.A1 and 142.A2 therefore assert on extra_fields.raw_request: taskType and title present on each of the three requests[] entries and absent at the top level. 142.A1 is the reporter's shape (OpenAI SDK extra_body => camelCase extra params; red pre-fix) with the typed task_type beside it: since TXE-7076 taskType alone is refused, because task_type is a price-affecting field (contract C4) and must show on the request. 142.A3 pins that refusal. 142.A2 is the first-class snake_case task_type/title, pinned so the two spellings cannot drift apart. Run with PROVIDER=gemini FEATURE="gemini-embedding-tasktype".

item.name: 142.A Request-level task type fans out to every :batchEmbedContents entry
142.A1 gemini/gemini-embedding-001 - request-level taskType beside the same task_type reaches every requests[] entry - #7812

body.raw:
{
  "model": "gemini/gemini-embedding-001",
  "input": [
    "Biodegradable Hydraulic Ester Fluid 46",
    "stainless steel ball valves",
    "contract manufacturing of injection moulded parts"
  ],
  "dimensions": 256,
  "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT",
  "taskType": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT",
  "title": "Industrial catalogue"
}
